examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Complex Conjugate of an Imaginary Number
examples.problem: What is the complex conjugate of $z=7\textrm{i}?$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate, we flip the sign of the imaginary part.

In the given number $z=7\textrm{i},$ the imaginary part is $7\textrm{i}$ (there is no real part, just an imaginary part). Flipping the sign, we get $-7\textrm{i}.$

Therefore, the complex conjugate is given by $\overline{z} = -7\textrm{i}.$

feedback.problem: What is the complex conjugate of $z=-3-7\text{i}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate, we flip the sign of the imaginary part.

In the given number $z=-3-7\text{i},$ the imaginary part is $-7\text{i}.$ Flipping the sign, we get $7\text{i}.$

Therefore, the complex conjugate is given by $\overset{―}{z}=-3+7\text{i}.$
